expanded_sentences: A 47-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of stage IV, T3, N1, M1 metastatic estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma with liver involvement, initially diagnosed as invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast at age 45.
The patient has a documented history of cancer-related fatigue with mild severity, reported as ongoing during systemic therapy, with onset at 46 years 8 months.
Liver metastasis was confirmed via biopsy at 46 years 6 months, with histology consistent with metastatic breast carcinoma.
Tumor profiling identified a PIK3CA mutation (c.3140A>G) in the primary breast lesion, which may influence targeted treatment selection.
The patient is currently receiving endocrine therapy with Fulvestrant (500 mg intramuscular) and Palbociclib (125 mg oral).
A core needle biopsy of the primary breast lesion confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma, while a hepatic core biopsy confirmed metastatic breast carcinoma.
A CA 15-3 measurement of 86.4 unit/mL was recorded during progression assessment.
The patient has a family history of breast carcinoma in a maternal aunt, diagnosed at age 52 years.
Magnetic Resonance Imaging was performed on 2026-02-18 for disease assessment.
